notes:
Circuit: series-shunt AC ladder. 5cos(200t) V source (V-AC #4) drives 2k series resistor (#1), 50uF shunt capacitor (#2) to ground, 2mH series inductor (#0), 20 ohm load resistor (#3) to ground; bottom rail is the common/ground rail. 6 components, 4 nets.

Net map:
  n3 = source top terminal (4.1) -> left lead of the 2k resistor (1.0): the wire up the left side from (236,474) to (346,378) and along the top rail to the resistor.
  n1 = middle top node: right lead of 2k resistor (1.1) at (450,380), top plate of the 50uF cap (2.0) at (501,458) via the vertical drop at x=503, and left lead of the 2mH inductor (0.0) at (545,376).
  n2 = right top node: right lead of the inductor (0.1) at (641,374), top of the 20 ohm resistor (3.0) at (741,464).
  0  = bottom/ground rail: source bottom (4.0), bottom of the 20 ohm resistor (3.1), bottom plate of the cap (2.1), and the GND symbol (5.0) hanging below the rail at (491,657).

Judgement calls:
  S9 (503,378) - CRITICAL, taken as JUNCTION. Pixel crop shows a clean T: the capacitor's vertical wire terminates on the horizontal top rail, no crossing branch above it. A crossing reading is not even available (deg=3). Junction is what makes the cap a shunt element between the R-L midpoint and ground.
  S10 (492,633) - CRITICAL, tracer default was CROSSING (it scored hop=8.1); OVERRIDDEN to JUNCTION. inkmap at (492,633) shows a plain X: the vertical cap-to-GND wire runs at x=494-495 above the rail, wobbles 2 px to x=492-493 around y=623-627 and continues straight down at x=492-493 below the rail at y=635+. That 2 px lateral wobble is pen drift, not a semicircular hop or a sideways jog, and there is no solder dot (the horizontal rail is 2-3 px thick at the crossing, same as everywhere else). Electrical impossibility settles it anyway: with a crossing, net 0 would contain only the GND symbol and the bottom cap plate, so the capacitor branch would have no return path (a dead-end series element carrying no current), and the source's return rail would be a floating net that never touches the ground symbol. As a junction the sheet reads as the standard textbook problem - a shunt C between the two series arms, everything referenced to the ground rail. Ink prior (plain X with no hop = junction on this dataset) agrees.
  Non-critical sites S0-S8 are all ink of the handwritten value labels '2K ohm' and '2mH' brushing the top rail and the component symbols; left at their defaults, they add no terminals to any net.

Port/terminal fixes:
  #1 Resistor (2k): terminal 0 moved from p4@(351,360) (wire len 6 - a stroke of the '2K ohm' label sitting just above the box) to p7@(346,378) (wire len 197 - the real left lead running to the source). Before the fix the tracer produced two one-terminal nets, n3={1.0} and n5={4.1}; they are the same wire, and the fix merges them.
  #0 Inductor (2mH): terminal 1 moved from p2@(644,364) (wire len 9 - the vertical stroke of the 'H' in '2mH') to p5@(641,374) (wire len 196 - the real right lead, edge e20 running to (741,464) = top of the 20 ohm resistor).
  bridges.drop [13]: bridge 13 joined (641,374) (the real inductor right lead) to (644,364) (the 'H' letter stroke) across a 10.4 px gap. With terminal 1 now pointing at the real lead the bridge is unnecessary, and keeping it would let label ink into net n2; the pixels show the lead wire and the letter are separate strokes.

Unresolved: nothing. Classes all confirmed from the comps montage (coil = Inductor, two zigzags = Resistors, two parallel plates = non-polarised Capacitor, circle-with-sine = V-AC, GND symbol).
